title: feat(types): declare `scale` on `PercentFieldMetadata` (objectui#9784)
body:
Fixes #9784

## What I did

I added `scale` to `PercentFieldMetadata` in `@object-ui/types`, copied verbatim from the
`NumberFieldMetadata` arm in the same module. **I did not touch `precision`** — see *Why
`precision` stays* below, which is a reading, not an omission.

Three files: the declaration (two lines), a pin under `packages/types/src/__tests__/`, and
a changeset.

⚠️ **On line addresses in this body.** AGENTS.md commandment #11 bans stored cross-file
`path:line` citations, and the dispatch asked for line numbers. Every address below is
therefore written as a **dated reading taken at commit `6b63264b11`**, ⛔ not as a live
pointer — the thing that re-derives each of these facts is the pin this PR adds, which
cites by content. Do not repair an address here; re-run the pin.

## The four legs, read at source on this branch

Base: `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` on my branch printed
`3ae740c4a8da5d8778e3290febb1fd2b1333fcce` — identical to the tip the dispatch quoted, and
computed rather than taken from it. The checkout is not shallow
(`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` prints `false`), so the history readings below
carry no shallow-window caveat.

### Leg 1 — the percent face declared `precision` / `min` / `max` and no `scale`

At the base commit, `PercentFieldMetadata` in `packages/types/src/field-types.ts` read:

```ts
export interface PercentFieldMetadata extends BaseFieldMetadata {
  type: 'percent';
  precision?: number;
  min?: number;
  max?: number;
}
```

⭐ **Lit control, same instrument and same corpus.** `grep -n "scale" packages/types/src/field-types.ts`
on the base commit returns **exactly one** hit — `  scale?: number;`, the member of
`NumberFieldMetadata` (dated address: line 409). So the instrument reads this file and the
zero on the percent arm above is a reading of absence, not a dead probe. That same control
leg is carried into the pin as a test case, so it keeps having to answer.

### Leg 2 — `PercentFieldMetadata` is published

`packages/types/src/index.ts` names it in the type-export block, verbatim on this branch:

```ts
  PercentFieldMetadata,
```

The package's `files` array ships `dist`, and after `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types build`
the emitted `packages/types/dist/field-types.d.ts` carries the new member with its
docblock. So this is a widening of a face consumers actually receive, not an internal note.

### Leg 3 — the percent CELL renderer reads `scale`

`packages/fields/src/index.tsx`, inside `PercentCellRenderer` (dated address: line 826):

```ts
  const scale = percentField.scale ?? 0;
```

Its own comment names the correction and the authority: *"Decimal places come from `scale`,
NOT `precision` — the same correction objectui#2131 made on the currency arm and
objectui#2134 on the number arm, arriving one type later (objectui#9295)"*, and it quotes
`@objectstack/spec` declaring `precision` as "Total digits (non-negative integer)" and
`scale` as "Decimal places (non-negative integer)". ⇒ An author who followed the published
type and wrote `precision` hit the `?? 0` branch and silently got zero decimals.

I read this file and did not write to it.

### Leg 4 — the second reader is an OPEN pull request, and I state it as such

⚠️ **This is a fact about a pull request, ⛔ not a fact about `main`.** I verified its state
myself rather than taking the dispatch's word: `GET /repos/objectstack-ai/objectui/pulls/9804`
answered `state: open`, `draft: false`, `merged: false`, head `2e421f196ecb`, base `main`,
titled *"fix(fields): the percent edit widget reads `scale` for its fraction width"*. So
**an open pull request has the percent EDIT widget reading `scale` too**; on `main` today
that second read does not yet exist. My pin deliberately does not assert anything about
that file, so nothing here races that branch.

### ⭐ A fifth reading the card did not carry — there is a THIRD reader, already on `main`

`packages/plugin-detail/src/DetailView.tsx` (dated address: line 1233) reads the same
member for the detail summary chip:

```ts
                        const scale = percentField.scale ?? 0;
```

Its comment routes the chip onto the list cell as the authority and records that the member
moved with objectui#9295. So the undeclared key had **two** readers on `main` (list cell +
detail chip) before the open pull request adds a third. That strengthens the card's premise;
it does not change the fix.

## Why `precision` stays — and why this is not a fork

The dispatch gave me an exit if I concluded `precision` could not stay alongside `scale`. **I
did not reach that conclusion, and here is what I read instead.**

The installed `@objectstack/spec` declares the two as a **pair on one field face** —
`FieldSchema` in `@objectstack/spec/data`, under a `Number Constraints` heading:

```ts
  precision: z.number().int().min(0).optional().describe('Total digits (non-negative integer)'),
  scale: z.number().int().min(0).optional().describe('Decimal places (non-negative integer)'),
```

And its door accepts both on a **percent** field document. Measured against the installed
spec on this branch, and pinned in the test:

| probe | `FieldSchema.safeParse` |
|---|---|
| a percent field carrying `scale: 2` | accepted |
| the same document carrying `precision: 10` | accepted |
| the same document carrying `scale: 2.5` | refused (a digit count is an integer) |
| the same document plus a bogus key | refused **by name**, `unrecognized_keys` |

That last row is the control: the door is strict, so the two acceptances above are readings
rather than a passthrough. ⇒ `precision` is a **spec-legal declaration on this face**, and
keeping it is the spec-conformant state under commandment #0 (spec declaration outranks
implementation). Narrowing or retiring it would move a published accept set against the
spec's own answer. ⛔ I did not narrow it, deprecate it, retire it or re-document it, and
this PR takes no position on whether it should ever move.

## Clause-②: yes, and the changeset says which face widened

The dispatching seat graded this `Clause-②: yes` on the carrier rule — a new key on a
published payload — and I re-declare it on the same ground, **independently of the key
already being read at runtime**. The authoring face genuinely widens: a
`PercentFieldMetadata` object literal carrying `scale` failed excess-property checking at the
base commit and type-checks after this lands. `BaseFieldMetadata` has no index signature, so
that check is real. The changeset names the widened face in those words and declares `minor`
(this repo's version policy forbids `major` in a changeset; `check:changeset-no-major` is
green).

`needs:contract-review` rides on this PR from the moment it exists. ⛔ I do not clear it —
that is the reviewing seat's act.

## The pin, and its ablation

`packages/types/src/__tests__/percent-field-metadata-scale-9784.test.ts`, in this package's
house form (the neighbour it copies is `field-metadata-depends-on-declared-6153.test.ts`).
It pins **substance on two instruments**, because membership pins here are type-level and do
not bite under the vitest runtime:

- **type-level** (bites under `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, this package's `type-check`
  chain): the invariant-equality helper asserts the percent `scale` is the same shape as the
  number arm's, an annotated literal carrying `scale` must compile, one carrying both digit
  counts must compile, and a near-miss spelling must still be refused.
- **runtime**: the declaration text and the parity of the `scale` docblock between the two
  arms, with the number arm as the control; that `precision` is still declared; the read
  site in the cell renderer; and the spec-door probe above with its bogus-key control.

⚠️ **Ablation — the pin was removed-tested from a committed state**, restored under a trap
with absolute paths, with the mutation proved on disk before either instrument ran:

```
HEAD blob = 0c8342c50bdb3fbe7db517b333e9d9880dadb7cb
BEFORE mutation: `grep -c 'Number of decimal places to display'` = 2
anchor replaced exactly once
AFTER  mutation: `grep -c 'Number of decimal places to display'` = 1   (the number arm's copy — the control — remains)
mutated blob = b043a3be4ba7bc7f35f6c599ffdc9edb513a1572   (differs from HEAD: the edit reached disk)

INSTRUMENT 1  vitest  exit=1   Test Files 1 failed (1) · Tests 2 failed | 8 passed (10)
   FAIL  ... > `PercentFieldMetadata` declares `scale`
   FAIL  ... > the `scale` docblock says the same thing on both arms
         AssertionError: the percent arm declares `scale` with no docblock: expected undefined to be defined

INSTRUMENT 2  tsc -p tsconfig.test.json  exit=2
   percent-field-metadata-scale-9784.test.ts(64,77): error TS2339: Property 'scale' does not exist on type 'PercentFieldMetadata'.
   percent-field-metadata-scale-9784.test.ts(66,77): error TS2339: Property 'scale' does not exist on type 'PercentFieldMetadata'.
   percent-field-metadata-scale-9784.test.ts(79,3): error TS2353: Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'scale' does not exist in type 'PercentFieldMetadata'.
```

Restoration proved by state, not by an exit code: `git diff HEAD` empty, working tree clean,
and `git hash-object packages/types/src/field-types.ts` back to
`0c8342c50bdb3fbe7db517b333e9d9880dadb7cb`.

⛔ Note the `AFTER` count is **1, not 0** — the docblock line I deleted from the percent arm
is byte-identical to the number arm's, which is the whole point of the parity pin, so the
surviving occurrence is the control. A `0` there would have meant I had ablated the control
too.

## Verification run on this branch

Repo-root invocation throughout, per AGENTS.md (⛔ never `cd` into the package for vitest).
Heavy runs went through the shared lock in the sibling checkout.

| what | command | result |
|---|---|---|
| the new pin | `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/src/__tests__/percent-field-metadata-scale-9784.test.ts` | `Test Files 1 passed (1)` · `Tests 10 passed (10)` |
| the whole affected package | `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/` | `Test Files 205 passed (205)` · `Tests 4787 passed (4787)` |
| type-check, incl. the type-level pins | `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check` | exit 0 |
| build + dist completeness | `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types build` | exit 0; the emitted `dist/field-types.d.ts` carries `scale` with its docblock |
| dependency closure | `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/types^...' build` | the closure is one private package with no `build` script ⇒ nothing to build, a genuine no-op, ⛔ not a pass |
| the downstream reader | `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/fields^...' build && pnpm --filter @object-ui/fields type-check` | exit 0. ⚠️ Run WITHOUT the closure build first, it reported eight `TS2307 Cannot find module` errors — a prerequisite miss, ⛔ not a red gate; the reading above is the one after the closure was built |
| lint, the touched files | `pnpm exec eslint` on the two touched source files, `--format json` | 0 errors. 6 pre-existing `no-explicit-any` **warnings**, all on lines my diff does not touch |
| derived gates | `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:designer-field-key-parity`, `check:unreferenced-sources` | all exit 0 |
| changeset gates | `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`, `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` | exit 0 · *"1 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)"* |
| governed surface | `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` on all three paths | *"NOT GOVERNED — 3 path(s) checked against 5 governed surface(s); none matched."* ⇒ ordinary review and merge-queue route |
| control bytes, by hand | `grep -naP` for the control-byte class over the three touched files | no hits |

⛔ **Not measured locally, declared to CI:** the repo-wide `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test` runs. I
did not narrow them — I did not run them at all, and CI owns that farm.

## Fences I was given, and what I did with them

- ⛔ `packages/fields/src/widgets/PercentField.tsx` — held by an open pull request. **Not
  read into the diff, not written.**
- ⛔ `packages/fields/src/index.tsx` — the subject of a separate open card. **Read only**;
  the pin on it asserts the read by content and deliberately tolerates the expression being
  reshaped around it, so a clamp landing there does not collide with this pin.
- ⛔ `precision` — untouched, with the spec reading above as the reason.

## Acceptance notes

**To file (⛔ not filed by me — for the triage seat, with dedupe words), one candidate:**

`CurrencyFieldMetadata` may carry the same defect class as this card. It declares
`currency` / `precision` / `min` / `max` and no `scale`, while the spec's field face declares
the pair, and `scale` is read off field/column definitions on currency-typed columns —
`packages/fields/src/widgets/GridField.tsx` resolves `scale` with a currency-specific
default, and `packages/plugin-grid/src/useColumnSummary.ts` reads it for the footer. ⚠️ **State
of the evidence, honestly**: every one of those reads reaches the member through an untyped
or cast carrier, ⛔ not through `CurrencyFieldMetadata`, and I took **no runtime reading** — so
this is a candidate for the grading seat, ⛔ not a graded finding, and AGENTS.md is explicit
that a source grep alone cannot settle whether a declared key is read. Dedupe words:
`CurrencyFieldMetadata`, `scale`, `precision`, `currency field metadata`, `decimal places`.

**Noted, ⛔ not filed:**

- `PercentFieldMetadata` carries no docblocks on `precision` / `min` / `max`, where the
  number arm documents its pair. A documentation nit, ⛔ not a defect — and re-documenting
  `precision` is fenced by this card's ruling anyway. Who will meet this file: whoever takes
  the `precision` question if it is ever opened; **otherwise: no one**.
- The percent cell renderer reaches its field through `const percentField = field as any;`.
  Declaring `scale` does not by itself retire that cast, so the cast survives this PR. Who
  will meet it: the open card against that same renderer. ⛔ Not mine to change under the
  fence.
